title: Hand written SVG icons and graphics
when: The page needs icons, a simple logo, badges or decorative drawings without image files or icon fonts.
prompt:
Goal: Crisp, small, accessible SVG drawn by hand on a consistent grid that inherits color and scales cleanly.
Steps:
1. Icons use viewBox="0 0 24 24" with no width or height in the markup; size them in CSS (1.5em).
2. Draw with primitives first (circle, rect with rx, line, polyline), paths only when needed, coordinates on whole or half units.
3. Set style: fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round".
4. Decorative: aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"; meaningful: role="img" plus a <title> first child or aria-label.
5. Icon buttons carry the name on the button (aria-label="Close") and hide the svg.
6. Repeated icons: a hidden sprite of <symbol id> with <use href="#id">; keep each under about 1 KB and check at 16 and 48 px.
Quality bar:
- A set shares stroke width, corners and optical size.
- Color follows currentColor, so dark mode just works.
- No raster data inside.
Pitfalls:
- Exported paths with eight decimals.
- Fixed width and height that refuse to scale.
- Meaningful graphics without a text alternative.
Verify:
- [ ] Every inline svg has aria-hidden, aria-label or a title.
- [ ] viewBox on every svg.
- [ ] currentColor for stroke or fill.
- [ ] Icon buttons have names.
Output: Inline svg in the HTML or an icons.svg sprite, plus sizing CSS.

examples.input: ícones de menu, fechar e busca sem usar imagem
examples.output: three 24x24 stroke icons with currentColor in a symbol sprite, buttons with aria-label
